heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini prints eSUN PETG seamlessly out of the box with its stock stainless steel nozzle and open-frame design. By tuning OrcaSlicer to a maximum volumetric flow of 14 mm³/s, you can safely sustain speeds up to 167 mm/s without compromising layer adhesion or surface finish.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of PVA glue stick or liquid glue as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 14 mm³/s under the Filament Settings tab to avoid underextrusion at high speeds.
Enable Wipe While Retracting with a 1.0 mm Wipe Distance to prevent PETG nozzle buildup and fine surface stringing.
Lower auxiliary fan speed to 0% and keep part cooling fan between 20% and 50% to maximize inter-layer adhesion.
Increase Pressure Advance to approximately 0.038-0.042 s for sharp corners without bulging, calibrated via OrcaSlicer PA Line test.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine whisker formation across open travels
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: eSUN PETG is hygroscopic and exhibits ooze-prone viscosity when moisture is absorbed or travel settings are unoptimized.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 hours; in OrcaSlicer, enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' and set retraction to 0.8 mm at 30 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Print tears the PEI coating off the flexible bed plate upon removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG bonds chemically to raw PEI surfaces when heated near its glass transition point.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of Bambu Liquid Glue or standard glue stick before printing to serve strictly as an interface release agent.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle parts and weak layer bonding on vertical perimeters
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or printing below the optimal melt temperature for PETG's polymer chains.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Raise nozzle printing temperature to 240°C, disable the aux chamber fan completely, and cap the part cooling fan at 40%.

faq.question: Can I print eSUN PETG on the A1 Mini without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes. PETG does not require an enclosure because its shrinkage rate is much lower than ABS or ASA, making the open-frame A1 Mini fully capable.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel hotend for eSUN PETG?
faq.answer: No. Standard eSUN PETG is non-abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle on the A1 Mini will handle it without accelerated wear.

faq.question: Why is the maximum recommended bed temperature set to 78°C instead of higher?
faq.answer: The A1 Mini has an 80°C hard bed temperature limit; setting the target to 78°C provides optimal thermal performance within a safe hardware margin.

faq.question: How do I dry eSUN PETG before printing on the A1 Mini?
faq.answer: Because the A1 Mini has an open frame and no heated chamber drying feature, use a dedicated filament dryer or food dehydrator at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours.
